paragraphs.en: As an {educator}, people often ask me how I know what is going on in the minds of my students. Many students are quite shy and don't speak all that much. At the same time, in a classroom of more than forty students, it is hard to have many one-on-one conversations with each person. So, how can I really know what makes each student {tick}?
paragraphs.cn: 作为一名教育工作者，人们常问我：我是怎么知道学生们心里在想什么的。许多学生相当害羞，话也不太多。同时，在四十多人的教室里，很难与每个人进行很多一对一的交谈。那么，我究竟是如何了解每个学生的心思的呢？

paragraphs.en: My answer? I look at their body language.
paragraphs.cn: 我的答案？我看他们的肢体语言。

paragraphs.en: It is easy to recognise when students are interested in a lesson. Most tend to look up and make eye contact. When I make a joke, they smile. When I talk about something difficult, they look confused. I know when students are really interested, however, because they lean forward and look at me. People have a tendency to lean towards whatever they are interested in. So if a student has his head lowered to look at his watch, it implies he is bored and just counting the minutes for the class to end.
paragraphs.cn: 当学生对一堂课感兴趣时，很容易辨认。大多数学生会抬起头、进行眼神交流。我讲笑话时，他们会微笑。我讲到难点时，他们会露出困惑的神情。不过，我知道学生何时真正感兴趣，是因为他们会身体前倾、望着我。人们往往会对自己感兴趣的事物倾身靠近。所以，如果一个学生低着头看手表，那就意味着他觉得无聊，只是在数着分钟等待下课。

paragraphs.en: If two friends are leaning their heads together, they are probably writing notes to each other. Of course, not everyone who looks up is paying attention in class. Some students look up, but there is an absence of eye contact. Their eyes {barely} move, and they always have the same distant expression on their faces. It is as though they are asleep with their eyes open.
paragraphs.cn: 如果两个朋友把头凑在一起，他们大概在互相写纸条。当然，并不是每个抬头的人都在专心听课。有些学生抬着头，却毫无眼神交流。他们的眼睛几乎不动，脸上始终带着同样疏离的表情，就好像睁着眼睛睡着了。

paragraphs.en: Some students are amused by something else. They spend all their time looking anywhere but at me. Then again, some students' favourite activity is daydreaming. With their chins on their hands, they {occupy} themselves by staring out of the window or up at the ceiling. They are certainly interested in something, but who knows what. The main thing is reminding distracted students that they need to pay attention in class.
paragraphs.cn: 有些学生被别的东西逗乐了。他们把所有时间都花在盯着除了我以外的任何地方。再说，有些学生最爱做的便是白日梦——他们手托下巴，盯着窗外或天花板来消磨时间。他们肯定对什么感兴趣，可谁知道是什么呢。关键在于提醒走神的学生：他们需要专心上课。

paragraphs.en: While it is easy to {perceive} when students are interested, bored, or distracted, it is sometimes much harder to {distinguish} when students are troubled. Students who are angry, afraid, or experiencing {anxiety} may have their arms crossed in front of their chests and their legs closed or crossed, like they are guarding their bodies. Students who are sad or worried will nearly always wear a frown. They may also hide their faces in their hands like they are embarrassed or {ashamed}. Some students act this way {merely} because they are afraid of being called on by the teacher. However, if a student does not {bother} to brush her hair and her eyes are red from weeping, then I can infer that there are deeper issues at work. It could be that she is having serious conflicts with other students or at home. Whatever it is, I know I need to {inquire} and assess what is going on.
paragraphs.cn: 虽然学生感兴趣、无聊或分心时很容易察觉，但有时要分辨学生何时"心烦"则要困难得多。生气、害怕或焦虑的学生可能会双臂交叉抱在胸前，双腿并拢或交叉，仿佛在保护自己的身体。悲伤或担忧的学生几乎总是皱着眉头。他们也可能用手捂住脸，像是感到尴尬或羞愧。有些学生这样做，仅仅是因为害怕被老师点名。然而，如果一个学生连头发都懒得梳，而且眼睛因哭泣而发红，那我就能推断背后有更深的问题。也许是她与同学或家里发生了严重冲突。不管是什么，我知道我需要去询问并评估究竟发生了什么。

paragraphs.en: {Ultimately}, my duty is helping every student learn. Their body language lets me know when to {adjust} class activities, when to {intervene}, and when to talk to students individually, so they can all get the most out of school. Reacting to body language is an important {component} of being a teacher.
paragraphs.cn: 最终，我的职责是帮助每个学生去学习。他们的肢体语言让我知道何时调整课堂活动、何时介入、何时与学生单独交谈，好让他们都能在学校里收获最多。对肢体语言作出反应，是作为一名教师的重要组成部分。

vocab.meaning: 教师；教育工作者；教育家
